text:
Predicates:
Zaha(x) ::: x is a Zaha Hadid's design style.
Kelly(x) ::: x is a Kelly Wearstler's design style.
Brutalist(x) ::: x is a brutalist building.
Adores(x, y) ::: x adores y.
Interesting(x) ::: x has interesting geometries.
Evocative(x) ::: x is evocative.
Dreamy(x) ::: x is dreamy.
Premises:
∀x (Zaha(x) ∧ Adores(max, x) → Interesting(x)) ::: All of Zaha Hadid's design styles that Max adores have interesting geometries.
∀x (Brutalist(x) ∧ Adores(max, x) → ¬Interesting(x)) ::: No brutalist buildings that Max adores have interesting geometries.
∀x (Adores(max, x) → Zaha(x) ∨ Kelly(x)) ::: Every style that Max adores is either Zaha Hadid's design style or Kelly Wearstler's design style.
∀x (Kelly(x) ∧ Adores(max, x) → Evocative(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles that Max adores are evocative.
∀x (Kelly(x) ∧ Adores(max, x) → Dreamy(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles that Max adores are dreamy.
∀x (Adores(max, x) ∧ Interesting(x) → Brutalist(x) ∧ Evocative(x)) ::: If a design by Max that he adores has interesting geometries, then the design is a brutalist building and evocative.
Conclusion:
∃x (Brutalist(x) ∧ Adores(max, x)) ::: A design by Max is a brutalist building.
